Consult Summary:
- Middle-aged woman (Mary Smith, DOB 16-Aug-1976) with ~2-week progressive left arm numbness/tingling (palmar digits 2–4) with subjective weakness and a transient ~20-minute left-eye visual loss; clinician arranged urgent neurology referral and brain imaging to evaluate causes including cervical radiculopathy, peripheral median nerve compression, and demyelinating disease (DDx-consistent).

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Progressive numbness/tingling of left upper limb for ~2 weeks, now with subjective weakness (difficulty with fine motor tasks such as piano; occasional dropping).
  - Sensory distribution: palmar (anterior) surface of left hand, affecting 2nd, 3rd and 4th digits; also numbness around elbow and along arm.
  - Transient visual disturbance: brief (~20 minutes) loss of part of vision in the left eye a few weeks ago, resolved.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began ~2 weeks after starting boxing classes; started as mild tingling and have gradually worsened to persistent numbness and weakness.
  - Transient visual event occurred a few weeks ago and resolved within ~20 minutes.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Symptoms associated with arm movement and boxing; patient tried massage and warm baths without improvement.
  - Took occasional ibuprofen for muscle/knuckle soreness; no benefit for numbness.
- Associated symptoms / system review:
  - Occasional shoulder pain with movement.
  - Intermittent fatigue; occasional tension-type headaches attributed to tiredness.
  - No seizures, no leg symptoms, gait/weight-bearing/walking reported as normal.
  - No nausea, vomiting, or acute severe headache reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No witnessed loss of consciousness or shaking movements.
  - No persistent eye symptoms now; transient visual loss resolved.
  - No prior chronic neurological diagnosis reported.
  - No documented systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss).

Past Medical History:
- Generally healthy according to patient.
- Recent viral/flu-like illness approximately 1 month ago (ill for ~2 weeks).
- No chronic neurological diagnoses reported.
- Family history: father with hypothyroidism and unspecified autoimmune disease; mother with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen — occasional for muscle/knuckle soreness (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Vitamin D — taking (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Melatonin — occasional for sleep (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- GP recommended iron supplements which patient mostly does not take.
- Allergies: No drug/food/environmental allergies mentioned in the transcript.

Social History:
- Recently started boxing classes (several weeks); reports repetitive upper-limb use and knuckle injury to right hand.
- One episode of heavy alcohol use ~1 month ago during an event; no chronic alcohol use reported.
- Right-handed. Works and exercises regularly.
- No tobacco or other substance use documented.

Family History:
- Father: hypothyroidism and "autoimmune stuff" (unspecified).
- Mother: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, high cholesterol.
- No other neurological family history reported.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Not recorded (no objective neurological exam documented in transcript).

Investigations:
- None performed or available in transcript.
- Clinician recommended an urgent neurology referral and a "brain scan and things like that" (imaging to be arranged by neurology).

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression:
- Working impression: focal left upper-limb sensory disturbance with subjective motor impairment, progressive over ~2 weeks, with a recent transient left-eye visual loss — urgent neurologic evaluation required to exclude structural (cervical radiculopathy, brachial plexus/traumatic neuropathy), peripheral median nerve compression, vascular events (TIA/amaurosis fugax, carotid dissection) and inflammatory/demyelinating disease (e.g., multiple sclerosis).

DDx Integration (top 2–3 aligned with transcript):
1. Cervical radiculopathy (high likelihood)
   - Supporting: progressive unilateral elbow/arm/hand sensory symptoms after starting vigorous arm activity; shoulder pain with movement; functional weakness affecting fine motor tasks.
   - Opposing: transient visual loss is not explained by isolated radiculopathy; no objective neck findings recorded.
2. Median neuropathy / peripheral median nerve compression (medium likelihood)
   - Supporting: palmar numbness of digits 2–4 fits median nerve distribution; repetitive hand/wrist use (boxing) could contribute.
   - Opposing: proximal elbow/arm symptoms and subjective weakness suggest a more proximal lesion.
3. Multiple sclerosis / demyelinating disease (medium likelihood)
   - Supporting: separated-in-time neurological events (transient visual disturbance then limb sensory/motor symptoms) in an adult woman; recent viral illness possibly preceding symptoms.
   - Opposing: visual event was brief (~20 minutes) and resolved quickly (optic neuritis typically longer); no objective neurological signs documented yet.

(Issues and plans below are based on the transcript and DDx; no new diagnostic test results are assumed.)

Issue 1: Progressive left upper-limb numbness and subjective weakness
- Assessment:
  - Differential includes cervical radiculopathy (mechanical), brachial plexus/traumatic neuropathy from boxing, and peripheral median nerve compression.
  - No objective exam findings documented; symptoms are progressive and affecting function.
- Plan:
  - Urgent neurology referral arranged (as per clinician).
  - Imaging: brain scan was specifically mentioned by clinician; neurology may request MRI brain and additional imaging including cervical spine imaging as clinically indicated.
  - Do not start disease-specific treatment empirically (steroids were discussed as possible therapy for certain diagnoses but were not prescribed; clinician stated treatment requires confirmed diagnosis).
  - Advise patient to avoid provocative activities (boxing) until specialist review.
  - Arrange prompt specialist review and document objective neurological examination (in clinic/neurology).

Issue 2: Transient left-eye visual loss (~20 minutes)
- Assessment:
  - Possible causes include amaurosis fugax / transient retinal ischemia or optic pathway involvement from demyelination (MS) — vascular causes (TIA) or carotid pathology also in differential.
- Plan:
  - Include this event in the urgent neurology referral for assessment.
  - Neurology/secondary care may consider vascular workup (e.g., carotid imaging) and neuroimaging based on their assessment.
  - Record and report any recurrence, progression, or new focal neurological symptoms immediately.

Issue 3: Possible inflammatory/demyelinating process or post-infectious neuropathy
- Assessment:
  - Recent viral illness and separated neurological events raise concern for inflammatory causes such as MS or post-infectious brachial neuritis (Parsonage-Turner).
- Plan:
  - Neurology referral and neuroimaging (MRI brain +/- orbits and cervical spine) to evaluate for demyelinating lesions.
  - If neurology confirms inflammatory demyelination, they may consider acute treatment (e.g., corticosteroids) and disease-specific management — not initiated in primary consult.
  - Document family history of autoimmune disease for specialist.

General plan / safety-netting:
- Seek immediate emergency care (A&E) if any of the following occur:
  - Rapid progression of weakness (including involvement of legs), new difficulty breathing or swallowing.
  - New or worsening severe headache, vomiting, loss of consciousness, seizure-like activity.
  - Recurrent or worsening visual loss.
- Avoid further strenuous or contact activities (boxing) until reviewed.
- Bring medication list and any prior medical records/imaging to neurology appointment.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No objective physical examination findings documented (no documented neurological exam, power, reflexes, sensory mapping, gait).
  - No vital signs recorded.
  - No investigations (imaging or labs) available at time of consult.
  - Medication doses/routes/frequencies not documented for ibuprofen, vitamin D, melatonin.
- Conflicts/ambiguities:
  - Neck pain: patient responses in the transcript are inconsistent (at one point appears to say "Yes, absolutely" to neck pain, later exchange is ambiguous) — conflict noted.
  - No direct contradictions between transcript and DDx content; DDx aligns with clinician concern and planned neurology referral.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall intelligible but contains occasional overlapping/ambiguous lines and pauses; some elements (neck pain) are unclear from the transcript.
